questions.stem: The value of $\operatorname{cosec} 10^\circ - \sqrt{3}\sec 10^\circ$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
$$\operatorname{cosec} 10^\circ - \sqrt{3}\sec 10^\circ = \frac{1}{\sin 10^\circ} - \frac{\sqrt{3}}{\cos 10^\circ} = \frac{1}{\sin 10^\circ} - \frac{\sin 60^\circ}{\cos 60^\circ \cos 10^\circ}$$
$$= \frac{\cos 60^\circ \cos 10^\circ - \sin 60^\circ \sin 10^\circ}{\sin 10^\circ \cos 10^\circ \cos 60} = \frac{\cos(70^\circ)}{\frac{1}{2}(2\sin 10^\circ \cos 10^\circ)\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)}$$
$$= \frac{4\cos 70^\circ}{\sin 20^\circ} = 4$$

questions.stem: The sum of all the roots of the equation $(x - 1)^{2} - 5|x - 1| + 6 = 0$, is :
The number of relations, defined on the set $\{a, b, c, d\}$, which are both reflexive and symmetric, is :
questions.solution:
Number of relations which are both which are both reflexive and symmetric $= 2^{\frac{n^{2} - n}{2}}$
(put $n = 4$)
$= 2^{6} = 64$

questions.stem: Let $f : R \to (0, \infty)$ be a twice differentiable function such that $f(3) = 18$, $f'(3) = 0$ and $f''(3) = 4$. Then $\lim_{x \to 1}\left(\log_{e}\left(\frac{f(2 + x)}{f(3)}\right)^{\frac{18}{(x - 1)^{2}}}\right)$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
$$L = \lim_{x \to 1}\frac{18}{(x - 1)^{2}}\ln\left(\frac{f(2 + x)}{f(3)}\right) = \frac{18}{(x - 1)^{2}}\left(\frac{f(2 + x)}{f(3)} - 1\right)$$
put $x = 1 + h$
$$L = \lim_{h \to 0}\frac{18\left(f(3 + h) - f(3)\right)}{f(3)h^{2}} = \lim_{h \to 0}\frac{f(3 + h) - f(3)}{h^{2}}$$
Use L'H
$$= \lim_{h \to 0}\frac{f'(3 + h)}{2h}$$
Use L'H
$$L = \lim_{h \to 0}\frac{f''(3 + h)}{2} = \frac{4}{2} = 2$$

questions.stem: Let the mean and variance of 7 observations $2, 4, 10, x, 12, 14, y$, $x > y$, be 8 and 16 respectively. Two numbers are chosen from $\{1, 2, 3, x - 4, y, 5\}$ one after another without replacement, then the probability, that the smaller number among the two chosen numbers is less than 4, is :

questions.solution:
$f(1) \ne 1$ and function should be one-one and increasing.
select 6 elements from co-domain (excluding 1)
Ans. $= {}^{8}C_{6} = 28$

questions.stem: The area of the region, inside the ellipse $x^{2} + 4y^{2} = 4$ and outside the region bounded by the curves $y = |x| - 1$ and $y = 1 - |x|$, is :
questions.solution:
[Figure: ellipse with the rhombus ABCD formed by $y = |x| - 1$ and $y = 1 - |x|$]
Required Area = Area of ellipse – area of rhombus ABCD
$= \pi(2)(1) - \frac{1}{2}(2)(2)$
$= 2\pi - 2$

questions.stem: Let $y = y(x)$ be the solution curve of the differential equation $(1 + x^{2})dy + (y - \tan^{-1}x)dx = 0$, $y(0) = 1$. Then the value of $y(1)$ is :
questions.solution:
$$(1 + x^{2})dy + (y - \tan^{-1}x)dx = 0 \Rightarrow \frac{dy}{dx} + \frac{y}{1 + x^{2}} = \frac{\tan^{-1}(x)}{1 + x^{2}}$$
$$\text{I.F.} = e^{\int \frac{dx}{1 + x^{2}}} = e^{\tan^{-1}(x)}$$
$$\int d\left(ye^{\tan^{-1}(x)}\right) = \int \frac{\tan^{-1}(x)}{1 + x^{2}}e^{\tan^{-1}(x)}dx$$
Put $\tan^{-1}x = t$
$\Rightarrow ye^{\tan^{-1}(x)} = \int te^{t}dt$
$= e^{t}(t - 1) + c$
$ye^{\tan^{-1}(x)} = e^{\tan^{-1}(x)}\left(\tan^{-1}(x) - 1\right) + c$
$\because y(0) = 1 \Rightarrow c = 2$
$ye^{\tan^{-1}(x)} = e^{\tan^{-1}(x)}\left(\tan^{-1}(x) - 1\right) + 2$
$y = \tan^{-1}(x) - 1 + 2e^{-\tan^{-1}(x)}$
$y(1) = \frac{\pi}{4} - 1 + 2e^{-\pi/4}$

questions.stem: The value of $\int_{-\pi/6}^{\pi/6}\left(\frac{\pi + 4x^{11}}{1 - \sin\left(|x| + \frac{\pi}{6}\right)}\right)dx$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
$$I = \int_{-\pi/6}^{\pi/6}\frac{\pi + 4x^{11}}{1 - \sin\left(|x| + \frac{\pi}{6}\right)}dx$$
$$I = \underbrace{\int_{-\pi/6}^{\pi/6}\frac{\pi}{1 - \sin\left(|x| + \frac{\pi}{6}\right)}dx}_{\text{Even}} + \underbrace{\int_{-\pi/6}^{\pi/6}\frac{4x^{11}}{1 - \sin\left(|x| + \frac{\pi}{6}\right)}dx}_{\text{Odd}}$$
$$= 2\int_{0}^{\pi/6}\frac{\pi}{1 - \sin(x + \pi/6)}dx + 0$$
put $x + \frac{\pi}{6} = t$
$$= 2\int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/3}\frac{\pi}{1 - \sin t}dt$$
$$= 2\pi\int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/3}\frac{1 + \sin t}{1 - \sin^{2}t}dt$$
$$= 2\pi\int_{\pi/6}^{\pi/3}\left(\sec^{2}t + \sec t\tan t\right)dt$$
$$= 2\pi[\tan t + \sec t]_{\pi/6}^{\pi/3}$$
$= 4\pi$

questions.stem:
Let $\vec{c}$ and $\vec{d}$ be vectors such that $\left|\vec{c} + \vec{d}\right| = \sqrt{29}$ and $\vec{c} \times \left(2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}\right) = \left(2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 4\hat{k}\right) \times \vec{d}$. If $\lambda_{1}, \lambda_{2}\ (\lambda_{1} > \lambda_{2})$ are the possible values of $\left(\vec{c} + \vec{d}\right) \cdot \left(-7\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}\right)$, then the equation
$$K^{2}x^{2} + (K^{2} - 5K + \lambda_{1})xy + \left(3K + \frac{\lambda_{2}}{2}\right)y^{2} - 8x + 12y + \lambda_{2} = 0$$
represents a circle, for K equal to :
questions.solution:
Let $2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + 4\hat{k} = \vec{a}$
$\vec{c} \times \vec{a} = \vec{a} \times \vec{d}$
$\left(\vec{c} + \vec{d}\right) \times \vec{a} = 0$
$\vec{c} + \vec{d} = \alpha\vec{a}$
$\left|\vec{c} + \vec{d}\right| = \sqrt{29} \Rightarrow \alpha = \pm 1$
$\left(\vec{c} + \vec{d}\right) \cdot \left(-7\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}\right) = \pm(4)$
$\Rightarrow \lambda_{1} = 4$ ; $\Rightarrow \lambda_{2} = -4$
If Equation $K^{2}x^{2} + (K^{2} - 5K + \lambda_{1})xy + \left(3K + \frac{\lambda_{2}}{2}\right)y^{2} - 8x + 12y + \lambda_{2} = 0$ represents a circle
coeffceint of $x^{2}$ = coefficient $y^{2}$ and coefficient $xy = 0$
$K^{2} = 3K - 2$ ; $K^{2} - 5K + 4 = 0$
$K = 1$ or $2$ ; $K = 1$ or $4$
$\Rightarrow K = 1$

questions.stem: If $x^{2} + x + 1 = 0$, then the value of $\left(x + \frac{1}{x}\right)^{4} + \left(x^{2} + \frac{1}{x^{2}}\right)^{4} + \left(x^{3} + \frac{1}{x^{3}}\right)^{4} + \ldots + \left(x^{25} + \frac{1}{x^{25}}\right)^{4}$ is :
If the coefficient of x in the expansion of $(ax^{2} + bx + c)(1 - 2x)^{26}$ is $-56$ and the coefficients of $x^{2}$ and $x^{3}$ are both zero, then $a + b + c$ is equal to :
Let the foci of a hyperbola coincide with the foci of the ellipse $\frac{x^{2}}{36} + \frac{y^{2}}{16} = 1$. If the eccentricity of the hyperbola is 5, then the length of its latus rectum is :
questions.solution:
$E : \frac{x^{2}}{36} + \frac{y^{2}}{16} = 1$
$H : \frac{x^{2}}{\alpha} - \frac{y^{2}}{20 - \alpha} = 1$ (Foci are same for ellipse and hyperbola)
$e = 5$
$$\sqrt{1 + \frac{20 - \alpha}{\alpha}} = 5$$
$$\frac{20 - \alpha}{\alpha} = 24$$
$$\Rightarrow \alpha = \frac{4}{5}$$
$$l_{LR} = \frac{2(20 - \alpha)}{\sqrt{\alpha}} = \frac{2\left(20 - \frac{4}{5}\right)}{2/\sqrt{5}}$$
$$= \frac{96}{\sqrt{5}}$$

questions.stem: If the domain of the function $f(x) = \cos^{-1}\left(\frac{2x - 5}{11 - 3x}\right) + \sin^{-1}\left(2x^{2} - 3x + 1\right)$ is the interval $[\alpha, \beta]$, then $\alpha + 2\beta$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
$-1 \le \frac{2x - 5}{11 - 3x} \le 1$ ; $-1 \le 2x^{2} - 3x + 1 \le 1$
$x \in \left(-\infty, \frac{16}{5}\right] \cup [6\infty)$ ; $x \in \left[0, \frac{3}{2}\right]$
$\Rightarrow x \in \left[0, \frac{3}{2}\right]$
$\Rightarrow \alpha = 0, \beta = \frac{3}{2}$

questions.stem: Let $(\alpha, \beta, \gamma)$ be the co-ordinates of the foot of the perpendicular drawn from the point $(5, 4, 2)$ on the line $\vec{r} = \left(-\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} + \hat{k}\right) + \lambda\left(2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - \hat{k}\right)$. Then the length of the projection of the vector $\alpha\hat{i} + \beta\hat{j} + \gamma\hat{k}$ on the vector $6\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$ is :
questions.solution:
[Figure: perpendicular from $P(5, 4, 2)$ meets the line $\vec{r} = (-1, 3, 1) + \lambda(2, 3, -1)$ at $N(\alpha, \beta, \gamma)$]
Let $N(-1 + 2\lambda, 3 + 3\lambda, 1 - \lambda)$
$\overrightarrow{PN} \cdot \left(2\hat{i} + 3\hat{j} - \hat{k}\right) = 0 \Rightarrow \lambda = 1$
$\Rightarrow N(1, 6, 0) \Rightarrow \alpha = 1, \beta = 6, \gamma = 0$
$$\text{projection} = \frac{\left(\alpha\hat{i} + \beta\hat{j} + \gamma\hat{k}\right) \cdot \left(6\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}\right)}{\sqrt{36 + 4 + 9}}$$
$$= \frac{6 + 12 + 0}{7} = \frac{18}{7}$$

questions.stem: Let PQ and MN be two straight lines touching the circle $x^{2} + y^{2} - 4x - 6y - 3 = 0$ at the points A and B respectively. Let O be the centre of the circle and $\angle AOB = \frac{\pi}{3}$. Then the locus of the point of intersection of the lines PQ and MN is :
questions.solution:
[Figure: tangents from $R(x, y)$ touch the circle with centre $O(2, 3)$ at A and B; angles $\pi/6$ and $\pi/3$ marked at O, $r = 4$] (R is point of intersection of tangents)
$$\cos\frac{\pi}{6} = \frac{r}{OR}$$
$$OR = \frac{2r}{\sqrt{3}}$$
$3(OR)^{2} = 4r^{2}$
$3(x - 2)^{2} + 3(y - 3)^{2} = 64$
$3x^{2} + 3y^{2} - 12x - 18y - 25 = 0$

questions.stem: Let O be the vertex of the parabola $x^{2} = 4y$ and Q be any point on it. Let the locus of the point P, which divides the line segment OQ internally in the ratio $2 : 3$ be the conic C. Then the equation of the chord of C, which is bisected at the point $(1, 2)$, is :
questions.solution:
[Figure: parabola with vertex O, point $Q(2t, t^{2})$ on it, and P dividing OQ in the ratio $2 : 3$]
$$P\left(\frac{4t}{5}, \frac{2t^{2}}{5}\right)$$
$$h = \frac{4t}{5}\ \&\ k = \frac{2t^{2}}{5}$$
Eliminate t
$$\left(\frac{5h}{4}\right)^{2} = \frac{5k}{2}$$
$5h^{2} = 8k$
$5x^{2} = 8y$
Equation of chord which is bisected at the point $(1, 2)$
$T = S_{1}$
$5x(1) + 4(y + 2) = 5 - 16$
$5x - 4y + 3 = 0$

questions.stem: Let $a_{1}, a_{2}, a_{3}, \ldots$ be a G.P. of increasing positive terms such that $a_{2}.a_{3}.a_{4} = 64$ and $a_{1} + a_{3} + a_{5} = \frac{813}{7}$. Then $a_{3} + a_{5} + a_{7}$ is equal to :

Let $\vec{a} = -\hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 2\hat{k}$, $\vec{b} = 8\hat{i} + 7\hat{j} - 3\hat{k}$ and $\vec{c}$ be a vector such that $\vec{a} \times \vec{c} = \vec{b}$. If $\vec{c} \cdot \left(\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}\right) = 4$, then $\left|\vec{a} + \vec{c}\right|^{2}$ is equal to :
questions.solution:
$\vec{a} \times \vec{c} = \vec{b} \Rightarrow \vec{a} \times (\vec{a} \times \vec{c}) = \vec{a} \times \vec{b}$
$\left(\vec{a} \cdot \vec{c}\right)\vec{a} - (\vec{a} \cdot \vec{a})\vec{c} = \vec{a} \times \vec{b}$ ; let $\left(\vec{a}.\vec{c}\right) = \lambda$
$$\frac{\lambda\vec{a} - \vec{a} \times \vec{b}}{9} = \vec{c}$$
$\vec{c} \cdot \left(\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}\right) = 4$
$\lambda\vec{a} \cdot \left(\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}\right) - (\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) \cdot \left(\hat{i} + \hat{j} + \hat{k}\right) = 36$
$\lambda(3) + 30 = 36 \Rightarrow \lambda = 2$
$$\vec{c} = \frac{2\vec{a} - \vec{a} \times \vec{b}}{9}$$
$\Rightarrow \vec{c} = 2\hat{i} - \hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$
$\Rightarrow \left|\vec{c} + \vec{a}\right| = \left|\hat{i} + \hat{j} + 5\hat{k}\right| = \sqrt{27}$

questions.stem: Let a point A lie between the parallel lines $L_{1}$ and $L_{2}$ such that its distances from $L_{1}$ and $L_{2}$ are 6 and 3 units, respectively. Then the area (in sq. units) of the equilateral triangle ABC, where the points B and C lie on the lines $L_{1}$ and $L_{2}$, respectively, is :
questions.solution:
[Figure: equilateral triangle of side a between the parallel lines, with A at distances 3 and 6 from the lines, angles $60^\circ$ and $\theta$ marked at the vertex on the lower line]
$$\sin\theta = \frac{6}{a}$$
$$\sin\left(60^\circ + \theta\right) = \frac{9}{a}$$
$$\sin 60^\circ\cos\theta + \cos 60^\circ\sin\theta = \frac{9}{a}$$
$$\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\sqrt{1 - \frac{36}{a^{2}}} + \frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{6}{a}\right) = \frac{9}{a}$$
$\Rightarrow a = \sqrt{84}$
$$\text{Area} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}a^{2} = 21\sqrt{3}$$

questions.stem: Let $f : R \to R$ be a twice differentiable function such that the quadratic equation $f(x)m^{2} - 2f'(x)m + f''(x) = 0$ in m, has two equal roots for every $x \in R$. If $f(0) = 1$, $f'(0) = 2$, and $(\alpha, \beta)$ is the largest interval in which the function $f(\log_{e}x - x)$ is increasing, then $\alpha + \beta$ is equal to ______.
questions.solution:
$D = 0 \Rightarrow \left(f'(x)\right)^{2} = f(x)f''(x)$
$$\frac{f'(x)}{f(x)} = \frac{f''(x)}{f'(x)}$$
$\ln c + \ln f(x) = \ln f'(x)$
$f'(x) = cf(x)$
$\because f(0) = 1, f'(0) = 2 \Rightarrow c = 2$
$f'(x) = 2f(x)$
$$\frac{dy}{dx} = 2y$$
$$\int\frac{dy}{y} = \int 2dx$$
$\ln y = 2x + \ln c_{1}$
$f(x) = y = c_{1}e^{2x}$
$\because f(0) = 1 \Rightarrow c_{1} = 1$
$\Rightarrow f(x) = e^{2x}$
Let $p(x) = f(\ln x - x)$
$p(x) = e^{2(\ln x - x)}$
$$p'(x) = 2e^{2(\ln x - x)}\left(\frac{1}{x} - x\right)$$
$$= 2e^{2(\ln x - x)}\left(\frac{1 - x^{2}}{x}\right)$$
[Sign scheme: $+$ on $(0, 1)$, $-$ after 1]
$\Rightarrow$ p is increasing in $x \in (0, 1)$
$\Rightarrow \alpha = 0, \beta = 1$

questions.stem: Let $a_{1} = 1$ and for $n \ge 1$, $a_{n+1} = \frac{1}{2}a_{n} + \frac{n^{2} - 2n - 1}{n^{2}(n + 1)^{2}}$. Then $\left|\sum_{n=1}^{\infty}\left(a_{n} - \frac{2}{n^{2}}\right)\right|$ is equal to ______.

Let $S = \{(m, n) : m, n \in \{1, 2, 3, \ldots\ldots, 50\}\}$. If the number of elements $(m, n)$ in S such that $6^{m} + 9^{n}$ is a multiple of 5 is p and the number of elements $(m, n)$ in S such that $m + n$ is a square of a prime number is q, then $p + q$ is equal to ______.
$6\int_{0}^{\pi}\left|(\sin 3x + \sin 2x + \sin x)\right|dx$ is equal to ______.
questions.solution:
$$= 6\int_{0}^{\pi}\left|2\sin 2x\cos x + \sin 2x\right|dx$$
$$= 6\int_{0}^{\pi}\left|4\sin x\cos^{2}x + 2\sin x\cos x\right|dx$$
$$= 12\int_{0}^{\pi}\sin x\left|2\cos^{2}x + \cos x\right|dx$$
$$= 12\int_{0}^{1}\left|2t^{2} + t\right|dt = 17$$

questions.stem: For some $\alpha, \beta \in R$, let $A = \begin{bmatrix} \alpha & 2 \\ 1 & 2 \end{bmatrix}$ and $B = \begin{bmatrix} 1 & 1 \\ 1 & \beta \end{bmatrix}$ be such that $A^{2} - 4A + 2I = B^{2} - 3B + I = O$. Then $\left(\det\left(\operatorname{adj}\left(A^{3} - B^{3}\right)\right)\right)^{2}$ is equal to ______.
questions.solution:
$A^{2} - (2 + \alpha)A + (2\alpha - 2)I = 0 \Rightarrow 2 + \alpha = 4 \Rightarrow \alpha = 2$
$B^{2} - (1 + \beta)B + (\beta - 1)I = 0 \Rightarrow 1 + \beta = 3 \Rightarrow \beta = 2$
$A^{2} - 4A + 2I = 0$ ; $B^{2} = 3B - I$
$A^{2} = 4A - 2I$ ; $B^{3} = 3B^{2} - B$
$A^{3} = 4A^{2} - 2A$ ; $= 3(3B - I) - B$
$= 4(4A - 2I) - 2A$ ; $B^{3} = 8B - 3I$
$A^{3} = 14A - 8I$
$A^{3} - B^{3} = 14A - 8B - 5I$
$$= \begin{bmatrix} 28 & 28 \\ 14 & 28 \end{bmatrix} - \begin{bmatrix} B & 8 \\ B & 16 \end{bmatrix} - \begin{bmatrix} 5 & 0 \\ 0 & 5 \end{bmatrix} = \begin{bmatrix} 15 & 20 \\ 6 & 7 \end{bmatrix}$$
$$\left|\operatorname{adj}\left(A^{3} - B^{3}\right)\right|^{2} = \left(\left|A^{3} - B^{3}\right|\right)^{2} = \left|A^{3} - B^{3}\right|^{2} = (15)^{2} = 225$$
